latestPosts.caption:
A while back I interviewed the great @kilianjornet, who mentioned that he thought I’d enjoy the challenge of a 24 hour run… 

I was immediately excited.

2 days later I started running my local track at 5pm. I ran all through the night and through the following day, finishing at 5pm, completing 4 marathons in the process. 

Don’t overthink things that you want to try. Just get on with it, embrace the pain and enjoy the experience.

latestPosts.caption:
Andreas Almgren spent his twenties fighting off injuries. Yesterday, on his marathon debut, he won New York.

At 23 he was coming off years of stress injuries and couldn’t break 1:50 for 800m, having run 1:45 at nineteen. His words were that he probably wasn’t going to reach world class, and hoped he might make a Swedish team again at some point.

At 31, he’s a major champion.

Seven years of pushing his threshold up session by session, engaging in long stretches of uninterrupted training and refusing to believe it was over. He broke 13 minutes for 5km in 2024, took World Championship bronze over 10km in 2025, won gold in the Half Marathon World Championships a few weeks ago and won in Central Park yesterday in 2:06:01.

Running doesn’t care what you managed at nineteen, or how promising you looked before your body stopped cooperating. It rewards the work you put in and the consistency you did it with.

There’s no shortcut version of that.
